summary: Numerical representations of text capturing semantic meaning, foundational to semantic search and RAG systems

content.overview: Vector embeddings are dense numerical representations (arrays of floats) that map text, images, or other data into high-dimensional vector space where semantically similar items are positioned close together. Unlike keyword matching ('cat' ≠ 'feline'), embeddings capture semantic relationships ('cat' ≈ 'feline' in vector space). Embeddings are foundational to semantic search and RAG systems, enabling LLMs to retrieve contextually relevant information. Generated by specialized models (not LLMs themselves), typical dimensions range from 256 to 3,072, with higher dimensions offering better accuracy but increased cost/latency.
keyPoints: Embeddings encode SEMANTIC meaning - 'dog' and 'puppy' have similar vectors despite different words; cosine similarity measures vector closeness (0-1 scale)
CRITICAL: Must use SAME embedding model for all vectors being compared - mixing models yields meaningless results (comparing apples to oranges)
Dimension tradeoff: Higher dimensions (1536-3072) = better semantic capture but slower search and more memory; lower (256-768) = faster but less nuanced
Embeddings are generated by specialized models (OpenAI text-embedding-3, Cohere Embed v3, BERT-based) - separate from LLM inference, separate API cost
Popular models (2025): OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (3072 dims), Cohere Embed v3, Mistral E5-mistral-7b-instruct - transformer-based, instruction-tuned
Vector similarity search uses ANN algorithms (FAISS, HNSW) for efficiency - exact nearest-neighbor is O(n), ANN is O(log n) with ~95%+ accuracy
Embeddings are FROZEN - once generated, vectors don't change unless text changes or model is updated (enables caching, precomputation)

examples.code:
// BAD: Using different models
query_vec = openai_model.encode("query")  // OpenAI embeddings

similarity(query_vec, doc_vecs)  // MEANINGLESS RESULTS!
examples.explanation: Different models use different vector spaces - comparisons across models are invalid

warnings: CRITICAL MODEL LOCK-IN: Changing embedding models requires re-embedding ALL documents - can be millions of vectors, significant cost/time
Embeddings don't capture keyword exactness - 'CEO John Smith' vs. 'CEO Jane Doe' may be semantically similar, missing the name difference
Higher dimensions aren't always better - beyond ~1536 dims, accuracy gains diminish while cost/latency increase significantly
Embeddings degrade for out-of-domain text - model trained on general text performs poorly on specialized jargon (medical, legal) without fine-tuning
Vector databases (Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma) add infrastructure complexity - not necessary for small datasets (<10K docs), consider trade-offs
Embedding generation costs scale linearly - embedding 1M documents with OpenAI text-embedding-3-large costs ~$130 (as of 2025)
bestPractices: Choose embedding model based on: (1) Domain (general vs. specialized), (2) Languages supported, (3) Dimension vs. latency tradeoff, (4) Cost at scale
For RAG: Use hybrid search (embeddings + keyword matching) - embeddings miss exact terms, keywords miss semantics; combine for best results
Cache embeddings aggressively - vectors are deterministic for same (text, model) pair, no need to re-embed identical content
Benchmark embedding models on YOUR data - general benchmarks don't always reflect domain-specific performance
Use approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search for >10K vectors - FAISS, HNSW offer 10-100x speedup with minimal accuracy loss
Version your embedding model in metadata - enables migration when upgrading models, tracks which vectors use which model
Monitor embedding API costs separately - can exceed LLM inference costs for large document collections
